Maria Gomez: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector change on prod yesterday, we're seeing a 6-9% drop in batch efficiency for long prompts. KV hit rate dropped from 87% -> 61% on the 16k prompt cohort. I pushed p95 traces to the perf dashboard. TL;DR: batching groups are mixing short decode-rate requests with slow long prompts, evicting KV entries.
Jun Park: Seen similar in staging. decode-rate buckets are wider than expected, so continuous-batching puts 1-token/fast decoders with 200-token slow decoders in same batch.
Alex Chen: Could be kernel fallback to slower matmul path — had a change to kernel selection thresholds. Maybe kernel picks different microkernels when batch has heterogeneous seq lengths.
Priya Sharma: Can we try stricter prompt-length bucketing + token budget per-cohort? Suggest target token budget 1024 for small, 4096 for mid, 16384 for long.
Maria Gomez: Proposed quick experiment: admission policy that enforces max token budget per batch and prefers KV-affinitized connections (session_id). If batch would exceed budget, open a microbatch.
Jun Park: I ran quick sim locally. With token budget enforcement at 4096, KV hit rate recovered to ~82% and latency p95 improved by 11%.
Alex Chen: Share sim details please — need config snippet to reproduce on canary.
Maria Gomez: ```
admission:
  token_budget_per_batch: 4096
  max_batch_size: 64
  prefer_kv_affinity: true
  kv_affinity_window_ms: 250
  decode_rate_bins: [fast, mid, slow]
  prompt_length_buckets: [0-64,65-512,513-8192,8193+]
```
Jun Park: Ran canary with these settings on rtx pooling. No regressions in throughput; kernel selection changed: fallback reduced.
Priya Sharma: We should add a decode-rate classifier metric to perf dashboard (bytes/sec inferred). Add alert if mixed-bucket batch ratio > 10%.
perf-bot: New alert rule 'mixed_batch_ratio' created by Maria Gomez. :white_check_mark:
